title: Context Platform Engineering to Reduce Token Anxiety — Val Bercovici, WEKA
talk_summary: WEKA presents context platform engineering: measure and maximize KV-cache hit rate by matching cache TTLs to agent request cadence and using memory tiers for self-hosted inference; they open-source a load generator for agent swarms with SLOs. Most results are vendor/infra-specific, but the cache-hit-rate framing and prompt-composition observations transfer to API-based agent orchestration.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat KV-cache hit rate as the key production metric and show that short cache TTLs cause repeated prefill when agent requests are spaced out.
takeaways.evidence_quote: KV cache hit rate is the single most important metric for production grade AI agents.
takeaways.numbers: Cache miss can cost ~10x input tokens; 1-minute TTL re-prefilled same tokens 15-16x.

takeaways.technique: Measure prompt composition and shrink tool-output churn
takeaways.what_they_do: They break down agentic prompts and find user input is small while tool use and tool responses dominate context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the rest of it is tool use and tool responses

takeaways.technique: Reuse enduring context for related subagents
takeaways.what_they_do: They distinguish short-lived subagents whose context does not endure from agents that keep context across wakeups, noting multi-agent common context affects token use.
takeaways.evidence_quote: These agents or these sub agents may be short-lived as in their context does not endure between one wake up and the next

takeaways.what_they_do: They show that sending the same logical context to an inference provider does not guarantee full cache hits, so cache locality matters.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you don't actually get 100% of the C hits that you could

takeaways.what_they_do: They open-source a load generator that simulates agent swarms and subtasks with configurable SLOs and deterministic/random prompt cycles.
takeaways.evidence_quote: configure agent swarms uh and agent subtasks with very specific SLOs
